groups.title: Engine and terminal
groups.note: The editor engine is Zed's, vendored at one commit and built into libthraggcore.so. The terminal is Termux's, vendored as two Gradle modules and built into libtermux.so.

components.name: Conquest Code
components.note: Thragg is a fork of Conquest Code, which supplies the editor, the Debian userland, the terminal, the LSP client, git and the ACP agent panel. Conquest Code in turn reuses Zed's engine crates and vendors Termux's terminal libraries.

components.name: Zed (engine crates)
components.note:
51 crate directories vendored at one commit and compiled into libthraggcore.so. They are split across two licences and each one is listed individually under Rust crates with its own — the GPL set is the editor proper (text, rope, language, lsp, worktree, settings, theme), the Apache set is gpui and its infrastructure (collections, util, sum_tree, http_client).

Four of them declare no license field in their Cargo.toml and are shown here with the licence file that is on disk beside them, per core/vendor/VENDOR.md: gpui_shared_string and gpui_util are Apache-2.0, grammars and language_core are GPL-3.0-or-later.

groups.title: Downloaded after installation
groups.note: Not in this package. Setup fetches each of these from that component's own upstream, onto your device, at your request; Eyed hosts none of them and mirrors none of them, so no source obligation attaches to Eyed for any of them. They are listed because they end up on the same phone and a reader looking for them should find them.

components.name: Debian userland
components.spdx: A collection of works under many licences
components.copyright: Copyright (C) the Debian contributors and upstream authors
components.note: Debian's own stable-slim container image, fetched from Debian's registry and verified against its digest. Every package in it carries its own copyright file at /usr/share/doc/<package>/copyright inside the installed rootfs, which is where its licence is to be read.

components.name: SBF platform-tools
components.copyright: Copyright (c) Anza Technology, Inc.; the LLVM Project
components.note: An LLVM with the SBF backend, and a Rust toolchain to drive it. The bundled LLVM is Apache-2.0 with the LLVM exception.

components.name: Spettro (the coding agent)
components.note: Eyed's own release artefact, fetched by default as part of Setup. Its licence has not been settled and this row says so rather than guessing: a stated licence that turns out to be wrong is worse than an honest blank. It is on the release checklist in docs/LICENSING.md.

components.name: Build tools (via apt)
components.spdx: Each package under its own terms
components.copyright: Copyright (C) the Debian contributors and upstream authors
components.note: The compiler and headers the two on-device crate builds need, installed by apt from Debian's own archives. Same answer as the userland: each package's copyright file is inside the rootfs.

components.name: cargo-build-sbf
components.note: Built on device from crates.io.

components.name: Anchor CLI
components.note: Built on device from crates.io. Anchor is also the shape the project scaffolds imitate — solana/templates/SolanaTemplates.kt writes an Anchor.toml, a crate manifest, a lib.rs and a test in the form `anchor init` produces, using Anchor's own placeholder program id.
